name: Noadiah
title: The Female Prophet Who Opposed Nehemiah
summary: Noadiah was a female prophet who lived during the time of Nehemiah, after the return from the Babylonian exile. She is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of those who tried to frighten Nehemiah and hinder the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. She represents one of the rare female prophets mentioned in the Old Testament, but in a negative context.

keyEvents.title: Noadiah Mentioned as an Opponent of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah asks God to remember the prophetess Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to frighten him from completing the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

keyEvents.title: Sanballat and Tobiah's Opposition
keyEvents.description: Noadiah operated in the context of the broader opposition from Sanballat, Tobiah, and other enemies who tried to stop the rebuilding work in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: False Prophets Try to Frighten Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah's enemies hired prophets, including Noadiah, to frighten him and make him commit actions that would discredit him. Shemaiah tried to lure Nehemiah into the temple to hide.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah's Prayer for Justice
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah asked God to remember Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and the other prophets who tried to frighten him, leaving judgment to God.

keyEvents.title: Completion of the Wall Despite Opposition
keyEvents.description: Despite Noadiah's and others' attempts to stop the work, Jerusalem's wall was completed in 52 days, causing the enemies to realize that the work had been done with God's help.
